_note: States with a mold disclosure or remediation statute. rule carries the citation inline.
_notice: General reference, not legal advice. Statutes change and vary by jurisdiction; verify every figure against the current official state code before relying on it. Last reviewed 2026-05.

CA.rule: Cal. Health & Safety Code § 26147 (Toxic Mold Protection Act) and Cal. Civ. Code § 1941.7: written disclosure of known visible mold to prospective and current tenants

FL.rule: Fla. Stat. § 83.51: mold covered under habitability; no specific statutory disclosure, but case law treats it as material defect

MD.rule: Md. Code, Real Prop. § 8-208.2: mold remediation by licensed contractor required; disclosure to prospective tenants

NJ.rule: N.J.A.C. 5:10-1 (housing code): mold treated as a habitability issue; disclosure required upon tenant inquiry

NY.rule: NY Lab. Law § 945 (Mold Assessment and Remediation Act): licensed mold assessor required for affected areas > 10 sq ft; NYC HMC § 27-2017.3 requires landlord remediation

TX.rule: Tex. Prop. Code § 92.024 and Tex. Occ. Code § 1958.154: mold remediation by licensed contractor required for affected areas > 25 sq ft; certificate of mold damage remediation required for prospective tenants

VA.rule: Va. Code § 55.1-1227: written disclosure of any known visible mold in unit; rental agreement must include 'mold provisions' if visible mold present at move-in

WA.rule: RCW 59.18.060(13): summary of state mold information must be provided to tenants at signing
